soleRemainingBarrier.claim: After this delta, `InsufficientPhUSDOut` (line 260) is the ONLY guard standing between a caller and a settlement in which the stablecoin half is consumed for less phUSD than it is worth — including for zero phUSD.
soleRemainingBarrier.basis: verified-by-reading. The two deleted guards were the only other value checks on that half: `expectedForStable == 0 -> PhUSDNotReceived` refused a zero-yield settlement outright, and `mintedForStable != expectedForStable -> PhUSDAmountMismatch` bound the outcome to the minter's own quote. Both are gone (git diff c91bc1a..3a96fb7). `calculateMintAmount` is now referenced NOWHERE in src/ or test/ (grep-verified, zero hits). The remaining guards at 254 and 256 are conservation checks about Antimatter's own balances, not value checks: 254 only says the stable left, 256 only says the phUSD balance did not fall.
soleRemainingBarrier.consequence-scope: Whether that is a defect depends on the minter's rate semantics and on caller behaviour — deferred to interaction/econ analysis. Recorded here as a verified structural property, prominently, because a downstream agent must not assume any protocol-side floor survives.

minPhUSDOutSemantics.asImplemented: line 259-260: totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable; revert iff totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut. The floor is on the COMBINED total of both halves, not on the stablecoin half alone.

unconditional1to1Half.claim: the antimatter half contributes exactly `amount` phUSD to totalPhUSD unconditionally
unconditional1to1Half.basis: verified-by-reading — `amount` is added verbatim at 259 and minted verbatim at 263 (_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)); no rate, no scaling, no branch sits between them. phUSD is 18-decimal (IFlax.sol:64) and antimatter is 18-decimal (OZ ERC20 default, no decimals() override in src/), so the 1:1 is dimensionally sound.

verifiedArithmeticProperty.statement: mintedForStable is uint256 and therefore >= 0, so totalPhUSD = amount + mintedForStable >= amount for EVERY reachable state. The predicate `totalPhUSD < minPhUSDOut` is therefore unsatisfiable whenever minPhUSDOut <= amount.
verifiedArithmeticProperty.inertRange: minPhUSDOut in [0, amount] — the guard can NEVER fire, regardless of the exchange rate, regardless of the minter's pause/cap/enabled state, regardless of the stablecoin's decimals. Passing any value in this range is exactly equivalent to passing 0.
verifiedArithmeticProperty.effectiveRange: minPhUSDOut in [amount + 1, type(uint256).max] — and within it, the protection actually purchased for the stablecoin half is exactly (minPhUSDOut - amount) phUSD, since that is the residual the stable half must clear.
verifiedArithmeticProperty.practicalConsequence: At a 1:1 rate an honest settlement returns 2*amount. A caller who reasons 'my floor is what my stablecoin half must fetch' and passes the stable-half figure (e.g. 100e18 against amount = 100e18) lands exactly on the inert boundary and buys ZERO protection while believing they are protected. Full protection of the stable half requires minPhUSDOut = amount + expectedStableHalf. The NatSpec at 222-225 does say 'in total, counting both halves', so the semantics are documented; the footgun is that the inert region is silent — an inert floor and an honoured floor are indistinguishable from the outside.
verifiedArithmeticProperty.boundaryIsInclusive: the comparison is strict `<`, so totalPhUSD == minPhUSDOut settles. Corroborated by test_floorMetExactlySucceeds (test/Annihilation.t.sol:348).
verifiedArithmeticProperty.overflow: 0.8.27 checked arithmetic; `amount + mintedForStable` at 259 reverts on overflow rather than wrapping to a small total that would spuriously trip the floor. No unchecked block anywhere in src/ (grep-verified).
verifiedArithmeticProperty.noCeiling: the guard is one-sided. A surplus above any expectation is forwarded in full to `recipient` (test_overPhUSDMintNowSucceeds, test/Annihilation.t.sol:335). The deleted PhUSDAmountMismatch was the only thing that had bounded the upside.

minPhUSDOutSemantics.zeroIsPermittedAndDocumented: NatSpec 224-225 explicitly sanctions minPhUSDOut == 0 as waiving the protection; test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor (test/Annihilation.t.sol:374) asserts that at a zero exchange rate the stable half is still taken and only the antimatter half is paid.
minPhUSDOutSemantics.handoffToInteractionAnalysis: Whether a caller-supplied, opt-out, combined-total floor is adequate protocol protection — given that the minter's exchange rate is owner-mutable (PhusdStableMinter.updateExchangeRate) and can move between quote and landing — is an interaction/econ question. Not adjudicated here.

toStableAmountReachability.question: is the story-002 decimals cross-check still reached unconditionally on the annihilate path?
evidence: Antimatter.sol:235 `uint256 stableAmount = toStableAmount(stable, amount);` sits in straight-line code with no enclosing conditional; the only way to reach 239 and beyond is through it.
It executes BEFORE _burn (239) and before every state-changing external call, so a failure there costs the caller nothing but gas.

The cross-check itself is intact and unmodified by this delta: 295 low-level staticcall to IERC20Metadata.decimals; 296 `if (!ok || data.length != 32) revert DecimalsUnavailable(stable)`; 297 decode as uint256; 298 `if (actualDecimals != decimals) revert DecimalsMismatch(...)`. git diff c91bc1a..3a96fb7 -- src/ shows zero changes below line 268.

Validation ordering is preserved and deliberate (comment 291-294): the two free checks first — yieldStrategy != 0 (288) and decimals <= 18 (289) — then the costly external call. Corroborated by test_unregisteredStableStillWinsOverDecimalsCheck (:582) and test_unsupportedDecimalsStillWinsOverDecimalsCheck (:590).
Decoding as uint256 rather than uint8 means a >255 answer fails the equality at 298 instead of reverting the decode uncatchably — test_toStableAmountRevertsOnDecimalsAboveUint8Range (:538).
Representability round-trip at 300-302 (`stableAmount * scale != amount -> AmountNotRepresentable`) is intact.
whatItStillDoesNotCover: config.enabled (struct index 3) is discarded at 287 — only yieldStrategy (0) and decimals (2) are destructured. A disabled stablecoin passes toStableAmount and is rejected only inside minter.mint (PhusdStableMinter.sol:209, 'Stablecoin minting is paused'), i.e. AFTER the burn but within the same reverting tx. Availability, not loss.

It reads `stable.decimals()` ONCE. A token that answers differently across calls within the same tx is not detected; the minter separately re-reads config.decimals inside calculateMintAmount (PhusdStableMinter.sol:254) — but note that Antimatter no longer calls calculateMintAmount at all after this delta.
It is `public view` and reverts on a codeless or unresponsive `stable` (test_toStableAmountRevertsOnCodelessStable :572), so off-chain quoting via this helper depends on the token being responsive.

PhusdStableMinter is owner-configured and honest. After this delta, the ONLY things Antimatter independently proves about it are: the phUSD wiring (checked at configuration time, 140-142 / 153-155), that the stable left Antimatter (254), and that Antimatter's phUSD balance did not fall (256).
